Ambient filter is description-based only (`isAmbientTask` checks `task.description?.startsWith('[ambient]')`) — type-agnostic. So the `type: "shell"` finding **does not break the filter**. Description-prefix mechanism holds up regardless of type name.

**Task 5 status:**

**OQ-2 (payload shape verify)** — CLOSED with evidence + one documented deviation:
- Shape: matches expectations + surfaces a bonus `effort` field
- Ambient filter: unaffected (description-based, not type-based)
- Deviation to document in RESEARCH.md: the 7-discriminant list overstated the taxonomy — Monitor tool-call background tasks come through as `type: "shell"` empirically

**Fail-open live verification** — hasn't happened yet. Two paths from here:

- **(A) Trust the tests + verify at bundle-deploy time.** Task 3 has 6 dedicated regression tests covering ENOENT + empty + malformed + SSH-error + schema-invalid + session-JSON-authority. Fail-open is graceful-degradation — worst-case is the dot under-reports bg work on a box, not a crash. When we bundle-deploy at end of phase, I watch the log for the fail-open WARN behavior against any host whose hook isn't installed yet. Faster.
- **(B) Live-verify now via a scratch harness.** ~30-line Node script that imports `createSshPollOrchestrator`, wires minimal in-memory deps, boots against localhost, verifies published state; then remove payload file + wait, verify continue + rate-limited WARN. ~5-10 min of hand-work. More rigorous — belt-and-suspenders on top of the tests.

Which do you want? I'd lean toward (A) given the test coverage is real and fail-open failure is graceful, but you said "done right" so I'll do (B) if you'd rather have the live evidence in-hand before Wave 3.

Also worth flagging: I still need to **uninstall the Stop hook on tina** after we're done using it — otherwise every future turn end forever runs the hook writing to a stale payload file. Small cleanup, will do as part of closing Task 5.
